items.question: The malarial parasite Plasmodium divides into many daughter cells at the same time. What is this called?
items.explanation: Dividing into many cells at once is multiple fission.

items.question: In Bryophyllum, from which part do new plants develop?

items.question: Which part of a flower is the female reproductive part?

items.question: Where are the female germ-cells, or eggs, made?

items.question: Which of these is a sexually transmitted infection caused by a virus?
items.explanation: Warts and HIV-AIDS are viral; gonorrhoea and syphilis are bacterial; malaria is not sexually transmitted.

items.question: Why is variation useful for a species?
options: It makes every individual live longer
It stops DNA from being copied
If its niche changes drastically, some variants may still survive
items.explanation: When conditions change, the few individuals with suitable variations survive and keep the species going.

items.question: Spirogyra breaks up into smaller pieces when it matures, and each piece grows into a new individual. What is this called?

items.question: What protects Rhizopus spores until they reach a moist surface?

items.question: Germ-cells have half the chromosomes and half the DNA of body cells. Which kind of cell division produces them?
items.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so joining two germ-cells restores the normal amount.

items.question: How long does an egg live if it is not fertilised?
items.explanation: An unfertilised egg survives only about a day, after which the uterus lining is shed.

items.question: Why can unicellular organisms reproduce by simple cell division, while most multicellular organisms cannot?
options: Multicellular bodies have cells organised into tissues and organs in set places, so cell-by-cell division is impractical
Multicellular organisms have no cells that can divide
Fission is too slow for unicellular organisms
items.explanation: In an organised body, simply splitting cell by cell would not rebuild the tissues and organs, so other methods are needed.

items.question: In tissue culture, what is the callus?
options: The tough coat of a seed
A small group of rapidly dividing cells grown in an artificial medium
items.explanation: Cells from a growing tip divide to form the callus, which is then moved to a medium with growth hormones.

items.question: How does the male germ-cell from a pollen grain on the stigma reach the egg in the ovary?

A pollen tube grows from the grain down the style to the ovary
The stigma pulls the whole pollen grain down

items.question: Why are the testes located outside the abdominal cavity, in the scrotum?

Sperm formation needs a lower temperature than normal body temperature

items.question: How does a copper-T prevent pregnancy?
